citation.title: Morality on the road: the ADC model in low-stakes traffic vignettes

reading.source_scope_note: Professional-philosophy respondents judge fictional human-driver traffic stories. Moral luck is explicitly explained as a limitation/secondary concept,not independently isolated as the experiment's mechanism. No AV decision system,real driving or machine moral agency is tested.
access_limits: All10extracted pages read,including sample exclusions,clustering,explicit repeated-measure methods,failed pet scenario,post-hoc restriction,limitations and references. Pages6–7visually inspected for condition estimates versus pairwise-table claims and scenario-fit results.
Complete vignette set,raw data,analysis code and external appendices were not obtained or rerun. Cited moral-luck primaries,PPIMTvalidation and books remain unread.
Metadata-only checks verified a mislinked Sütfeld response versus original paper,Leiner's volume/pages and original-versus-correction Dubljević DOIs. These are not additional full-text reviews.

study.sample: Self-selected philosophy mailing-list/department recruitment;at least master's degree,primarilyNorthAmerica
study.design: Random assignment toone of8valence combinations ineach of2human-driver stories,with scenario order randomized;two scenario ratings per person
study.outcome: Average personal and perceived-social acceptability,1–10;reportedR².825between the two
study.analysis: Methods explicitly state repeated-measures/mixed models;scenario-specific models and exploratory individual-weight regressions also described

summary: Add moral luck with an explicit focus on outcome-dependent moral evaluation beyond control,distinct from outcome bias and hindsight. Add a third fully read source to character-based moral judgment,while preserving the failed pet scenario and exploratory restriction. Record measurement/identifiability and citation corrections;do not infer AV moral agency or a universal expert consensus.

findings.definition: Differences in moral evaluation that depend on outcomes beyond an actor's control,despite otherwise comparable choices or risks.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Explicit secondary discussion of outcome-based moral luck in a read empirical article;the study does not independently isolate exante risk,control or the mechanism
findings.ai_proposal: Compare AI evaluations of agents who took matched risks with the same information and control but experienced different chance outcomes. Separately ask about decision quality,foreseeability,responsibility,blame and compensation,and require reasons for any difference rather than presuming every outcome-sensitive judgment is erroneous.
findings.novelty_rationale: Related to outcome bias but focuses on moral evaluation/responsibility shaped by uncontrollable luck,not only assessment of decision quality. Hindsight concerns perceived prior foreseeability. This entry covers the outcome-based form discussed here,not a new duplicate of every outcome effect.

evidence.quote: decisions result in bad outcomes due to unfortunate circumstances

findings.evidence_scope: The limitations section explicitly explains moral luck using lucky/unlucky drivers making the same risky decisions,citing Kneer/Machery2019andKneer/Skoczen2023. Those original texts are not read here. The present study varies final outcomes and overall acceptability rather than separately measuring uncontrollable luck and perceived negligence.
findings.boundary: Outcome-sensitive sanctions,compensation or moral judgments may have defensible reasons;the ethical status of moral luck is contested. Keep actual causation,control,foreseeability,intent and responsibility separate. This source addresses outcome luck,not every philosophical subtype or AI subjective culpability. An outcome effect alone does not establish a bias or unique psychological mechanism.

findings.term: Character information contributes to these traffic evaluations
findings.definition: A caring/abusive parent or compassionate/resentful driver description changes human moral evaluation alongside rule adherence and final outcomes,in a task with pronounced scenario differences.
findings.novelty_rationale: A third fully read relevant source for the existing construct,not another entry for the same ADCframework. This is the earlier primary experiment referenced byPDF0077.

evidence.quote: the protagonist driver is either a caring (A+)

findings.evidence_scope: 274philosophy respondents,two textual scenarios,each with8valence combinations. Explicit mixed/repeated-measure methods;overallAgentF15.25,p<.0001. Petmodel fails and is then dropped;Intersection-onlyreanalysis is exploratory.
findings.boundary: Norm-relevant intent,prior cruelty and stable character are bundled. Character effects are not automatically bias,objective ethical validity or proof that an AV has virtue. Do not generalize a successful scenario over the failed one or infer universal expert agreement.

findings.term: Moral luck concerns differ from a pure decision-quality outcome-bias test
findings.definition: Judging a completed event more favorably when the outcome is good does not alone show an incorrect assessment of the original choice under the same known risks.
findings.novelty_rationale: A discriminant boundary connecting the new moral-luck entry without falsely counting the same overall acceptability measure as a separate outcome-bias experiment.

evidence.quote: display actual consequences rather than the risk of collision

findings.evidence_scope: Consequences are described after the maneuver;predecision uncertainty and risk are not independently specified or measured.
findings.boundary: Outcome evaluation,decision quality,negligence,causal responsibility and hindsight are different. A bad outcome can be relevant to some judgments without showing the choice was foreseeably worse.

findings.term: Actor-observer explanations are background,not a directly tested attribution error
findings.definition: The limitations warn that external observers may overattribute traffic events to driver traits while underweighting circumstances,but no actor-versus-observer attribution comparison is performed.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keeps the existing disposition/situation construct separate from the mere presence of character cues and from the new outcome-luck concept.

evidence.quote: underestimate the circumstances in which an accident occurs

findings.evidence_scope: Participants are third-person observers of human-driver vignettes;they do not report their own driving-event explanations under matched conditions.
findings.boundary: A relevant character or intent cue is not automatically a fundamental attribution error. This source cites an actor-observer account secondarily;the distinct constructs should not be made synonyms.

findings.term: Constant survey answers can reflect conviction as well as low effort
findings.definition: Excluding respondents who give the same PPIMT or moral-judgment rating assumes careless responding,but can also remove coherent moral pluralism or equal judgments.
findings.novelty_rationale: Extends the prior survey-proxy boundary;the paper itself acknowledges firm conviction as an alternative. No new satisficing behavior or empirical evidence of early task abandonment.

evidence.quote: uniformity could, in theory, reflect firm conviction

findings.evidence_scope: 32of306completed responses are removed for constant answers across PPIMT or moral-judgment items. Only two scenario judgments are given perperson.
findings.boundary: A completed survey with equal responses is not itself low effort. Filtering a moral outcome can alter estimates and framework composition;the stated assumption of improved validity needs independent response-quality evidence.

methodological_limits: The methods explicitly describe repeated-measures/mixed models for two ratings per person;do not automatically apply the independent-row critique from other papers. Exact random/covariance structures and full output still require code for reproduction.

Each person rates only two scenario vignettes. The reported individual-level regressions estimating separateAgent,DeedandConsequenceweights cannot identify three unrestricted slopes plus intercept from two independent predictor rows. Constraints,partial pooling or a different data structure would need explicit specification.

The Pet/Dogmodel is nonsignificant withR².08and is dropped before the final exploratory analyses. Restricting to the better-fitting Intersection scenario does not independently establish robustness or generality across scenarios.

Figure1Petmeans show large component/combination differences,while the scenario-specific full model is described as poor/non-significant. Exact model/sample mapping and estimates require clarification;do not infer invented data or silently suppress either report.

Tables3and4are titled pairwise comparisons but list four condition estimates rather than the six pairwise differences among four combinations. Their uniformly smallpvalues do not by themselves document that all pairwise condition contrasts differ.

Framework classification forces threeKmeansclusters to match preferred theories,then checks their input dimension means. Such separation is not independent validation of philosophical commitments or evidence of three natural categories.

The overallPPIMTalpha.635is not a full subscale-validity analysis. Because the instrument is multidimensional,neither a single alpha nor prior validation ensures accurate individual dominant-framework classification in this sample.

The virtue cluster has high scores on all dimensions;other groups may differ in level as well as relative theory preference. Measurement equivalence,classification uncertainty and misclassification effects are not fully documented.

No detected Framework-by-component interaction does not establish theoretical equivalence,a universal moral core or broad societal consensus. Power,small deontologyN37and classification noise limit interpretation.

Thirty-two constant responders are removed partly using moral-judgment outputs;with only two scenario ratings,legitimate equal evaluations can be excluded. Constancy on preference items can also reflect genuine pluralism. No independent attention/effort measure validates every exclusion.

Subjects self-select from philosophy lists/departments;having a master's degree is not a probability sample of all expert ethicists,drivers or affected road users. Nonresponse and demographic skew limit generality.

Positive/negative character,rule and outcome manipulations differ in salience and substantive meaning. Coefficients do not reveal an intrinsic universal weighting of virtue,deontology and consequentialism.

Pearson association reported asR².825does not by itself prove personal and perceived-social acceptability are the same latent construct or have agreement. Averaging changes the target and can hide systematic differences.

Actual outcomes are shown without independently controlled expected risk,so consequence effects can include changed beliefs about prior negligence,causation or scenario comprehension. The authors acknowledge moral luck rather than claim it isolated.

The study does not test an autonomous vehicle. Characters are humans with human traits;the proposed numerical0–1ethical settings and future AV application are design suggestions,not validated implementations.

Judgment of a completed situation,choice during driving,public acceptance,legal compliance and objective ethical correctness remain separate. Descriptive consensus does not by itself authorize a normative algorithm or demonstrate machine moral agency.

Interaction analyses,scenario-specific reanalysis and post-hoc tests increase flexibility. A stated Tukey procedure is useful,but the reported tables do not expose all corresponding contrasts;no preregistration was identified in the supplied PDF.

Some statistical labels/estimates are incomplete or unclear:the validation section omits theAgentmean difference and has malformedDeednotation;the reportedF(1,259)=6.54,p.009also needs reconciliation under the stateddf. No estimate or p value is guessed.

Method terminology alternates Pet/Dogand contains a quasi-experiment description based on nonrandom sampling,although vignette assignment is randomized. Sampling and treatment randomization are separate;do not misclassify all causal contrasts solely from that label.
The paper recognizes that text/VR modes and first/third-person perspectives may differ. More immersion is proposed,not empirically shown here to improve real-world ethical validity.
Primary texts on moral luck,outcome effects,agency attribution,PPIMTvalidation and external datasets remain unread. Correcting citation metadata is not reading or reproducing those sources.

cross_paper_learning.finding: This earlier primary study supports character/rule/outcome effects but drops a failed Pet scenario. The later2026paper does not universally reproduce the rule result:textual rule effects reverse. Keep the empirical chain with task and analysis differences rather than claim identical successful replication.

The later paper's bibliography links Dubljević2018title toDOI10.1371/journal.pone.0206750,which Crossref identifies as a correction. The original is10.1371/journal.pone.0204631,as listed here. Link main article and correction distinctly;neither text has been independently read.

Knowing actual outcomes is not the same as comparing stated prognostic accuracy. Different normative and measurement targets prevent automatically treating every outcome-sensitive moral rating as a bias.

Agency attribution,error about control and moral luck are distinct:one concerns cue-based control inference,another outcome-dependent evaluation despite matched control. Both require direct measures before asserting a causal explanation.

deferred.reason: A framework already represented through existing categories and character-judgment notes,not an independent newly observed defect.
Secondary frameworks briefly summarized;not direct empirical mechanisms or separate behaviors isolated by this study.
Proposed explanation for interactions,not an independently measured expectation process. Read a primary operational treatment before a new mechanism entry.
A speculative extrapolation from null framework moderation,selected philosophers and one successful scenario,not an established behavior or ethical standard.
